nodes.label: You
nodes.role: installs it, runs its commands, hears it
nodes.summary: Runs agent-voice commands and hears the result.
nodes.detail: Installs with uv, runs install-skill / install-hooks, mutes for meetings, reads `doctor`. Approves and answers agent prompts at the keyboard — which is why alerts are chimes by default.

nodes.label: Claude Code
nodes.role: reads the skill, speaks, sends hook events
nodes.summary: Loads the skill, runs `agent-voice say`, fires hooks.
nodes.detail: Reads SKILL.md from ~/.claude/skills and calls `agent-voice say` through its Bash tool. Its PermissionRequest hook fires when an approval dialog opens — its question tool (AskUserQuestion) goes through it too. With --speak, PostToolUse, PostToolUseFailure, UserPromptSubmit and Stop fire the cancels. Hooks get the event as JSON on stdin and treat stdout as a verdict.

nodes.label: Copilot CLI
nodes.role: reads the skill, speaks, sends hook events
nodes.summary: Loads the skill, runs `agent-voice say`, fires notification hooks.
nodes.detail: Reads SKILL.md from ~/.copilot/skills. Its `notification` hook carries notification_type permission_prompt (approval) or elicitation_dialog (assumed to be a question — undocumented, unconfirmed). Its payloads don't name their event, so installed commands pass --event.

nodes.label: Copilot in VS Code
nodes.summary: Loads the skill only.
nodes.detail: Reads ~/.claude/skills and ~/.copilot/skills (so it lists the skill twice). Has no approval event, so gets no hooks.

nodes.label: uv + GitHub
nodes.summary: `uv tool install git+https://github.com/hevi-public/agent-voice`.
nodes.detail: Installs into ~/.local/share/uv/tools/agent-voice, links ~/.local/bin/agent-voice. About 1 GB of packages. Installs from git, not PyPI, because the spaCy model is a direct-URL dependency, which PyPI rejects.

nodes.label: macOS audio
nodes.role: plays the speech and the chimes
nodes.summary: /usr/bin/afplay plays WAVs and chimes; /usr/bin/say is the fallback voice.
nodes.detail: Every sound leaves through a subprocess: afplay for Kokoro's WAV and for the Glass/Ping chimes, say when Kokoro can't run.

nodes.label: ~/.agent-voice
nodes.role: locks, the server socket, mute flag
nodes.summary: playback.lock · server.lock · voice.sock · muted · hook-log files.
nodes.detail: AGENT_VOICE_HOME moves it. playback.lock serialises sound across processes; server.lock keeps one server; voice.sock (0600) is the server's socket, removed when it quits; muted exists only while muted; hook-log-on / hooks.log only while logging.

nodes.label: Agent config
nodes.summary: settings.json (edited!), skills folders, Copilot hook file.
nodes.detail: The only file agent-voice edits rather than owns is ~/.claude/settings.json — merged atomically, backed up once, left untouched when it isn't valid JSON. Everything else here is agent-voice's own file.

nodes.label: Hugging Face

nodes.label: mlx-audio · Kokoro
nodes.summary: Kokoro-82M on Apple Silicon via MLX.
nodes.detail: load_model() builds the model once per process (the voice server keeps it warm); model.generate() yields audio segments. A cold first sentence costs ~3.5 s, a warm one ~0.35 s.

nodes.label: spaCy · espeak-ng

steps.text: An agent decides to speak and runs `agent-voice say "…"` through its shell tool — the skill told it when and how.
cli.main routes to _run_say. It sets HF_HUB_OFFLINE so nothing reaches the network, reads the text (arguments or stdin) and checks mute.
_say_via_server hands the text to server.speak, which starts the voice server on first use (a detached `agent-voice serve`) and waits until it answers.
The client sends one JSON line over ~/.agent-voice/voice.sock. In the server process, the handler turns it into a Job and queues it — one speaker at a time.
The worker (main thread, where MLX is happiest) takes the job and calls speech.synthesize with the model already warm.

synthesize guards espeak's 159-byte path limit, maps the voice to a language, loads Kokoro once (cache only — never downloads) and runs model.generate: misaki and spaCy turn text into phonemes, espeak fills in unknown words.
The samples become a temp WAV (soundfile), and afplay plays it under playback.lock so two agents never talk over each other. Warm, sound starts ~0.4 s after the request.
The reply ({engine: kokoro}) goes back to the waiting `say`, which exits. If anything failed, macOS `say` spoke instead — see “What if Kokoro fails?”.

tours.title: What happens when an agent needs approval?

steps.text: An approval dialog (or a question) opens. Claude Code fires PermissionRequest; Copilot CLI fires a notification with permission_prompt or elicitation_dialog.

The agent runs the installed command `agent-voice hook --from claude --event PermissionRequest` with the event as JSON on stdin. It never prints and always exits 0 — stdout would be read as a verdict on the tool call.
handle logs the event name if hook-log is on (names only), then prompt_kind decides: approval, question, or nothing to do.
By default it chimes — Glass for an approval, Ping for a question — with a detached afplay, then returns in ~50 ms. You have to come to the keyboard anyway; a chime says enough.

With --speak, announcement builds the sentence: the tool kind from the agent's own tool name and the project's name (the main repo's, even from a worktree). Never the command — a partial read-out would make the rest sound safe.
It's queued on the voice server without waiting, tagged session:tool. No server? A detached `say` process speaks it instead.

Neither agent reports that a prompt was answered, so the next event does: the tool finishing, you typing, or the turn ending. handle sends cancel(tag); the server drops it from the queue or terminates the playing afplay.
That's why --speak installs extra hooks (PostToolUse, UserPromptSubmit, Stop …) and the chime default doesn't: a chime is over in a second.
install checks each agent's folder. A missing ~/.claude or ~/.copilot is skipped, never created; if none exists it fails before writing anything.
settings.json is the one file agent-voice edits rather than owns. If it isn't valid JSON, the install stops and leaves it untouched.
Old agent-voice entries (from any version) are removed first — only ours, recognised by the command itself; your own hooks stay.
The new command uses agent-voice's absolute path (an agent launched from the Dock may not have ~/.local/bin on PATH), quoted if it contains spaces.
A backup is copied once (settings.json.agent-voice-backup), then the file is written atomically: temp file, then rename. Copilot gets its own file, so nothing of yours is edited there.

tours.title: When does it touch the network?

steps.text: Install time: uv fetches the package from GitHub and ~1 GB of dependencies, including the spaCy model by direct URL — the reason it isn't on PyPI.
`agent-voice prefetch` is the only runtime path that downloads: model_path(download=True) fetches Kokoro (~340 MB) from Hugging Face into its cache.
Speaking reads the cache only (local_files_only) and `say` sets HF_HUB_OFFLINE, so huggingface_hub and transformers refuse to try. Tested with the network blocked.
No voice server (AGENT_VOICE_SERVER=0, a socket path over 104 bytes, or it won't start)? `say` speaks in-process instead.
Installed too deep for espeak-ng? That would kill the process silently, so it's refused up front with a VoiceError that names the fix.
Any Kokoro failure — missing model, bad voice, espeak — falls back to macOS `say`, and stderr says why. `--no-fallback` raises instead.
Hooks degrade the same way: no server → a detached process speaks. And every hook exits 0 whatever happens, so the agent is never affected.

tours.title: How does the agent learn to speak?

steps.text: install-skill copies the bundled SKILL.md into ~/.claude/skills and ~/.copilot/skills — only where the agent's folder exists, and never over a copy you've edited.

The agent loads SKILL.md when its description matches — or when you type /agent-voice conversational or /agent-voice announcer. The mode word is read from the invocation, so no agent-specific syntax is needed.
To make every session use it, install-skill prints an always-on line for CLAUDE.md and a Copilot instructions file — printed, never written: they're your files.
Born on the first `say`: start spawns a detached `agent-voice serve` and waits until it answers a ping.
serve takes server.lock (a second server just exits), replaces a stale socket, binds voice.sock with mode 0600 and warms Kokoro before the first request.
It speaks one job at a time for as long as requests come. After 30 idle minutes (AGENT_VOICE_IDLE) the loop ends, freeing ~780 MB.
`agent-voice stop` ends it at once; `doctor` shows whether it runs. On exit it removes its socket — only the two lock files stay.
